```{r}
grambank_languages <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-11-03/grambank_languages.csv")
```

#How similar are languages structurally across families and macro-regions?

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
family_names<-grambank_languages|>
filter(!is.na(longitude),!is.na(latitude),!is.na(family_name))|>
  group_by(family_name)|>
  count()|>
  summarise(total_families=sum(n))|>
 arrange(desc(total_families))|>
  slice_head(n=15)
family_names

data<-grambank_languages|>
  semi_join(family_names,by="family_name")|>
  count(family_name,macroarea)|>
  arrange(desc(n))|>
slice_head(n=15)
  
data
 
  


 
```

```{r}
data |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = n,
    y = reorder(family_name, n),
    fill = macroarea
  )) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.75,
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.2
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of languages",
    y = "Language family",
    fill = "Geographical region",
    title = "How Are Language Families Distributed Across Regions?",
    subtitle = "Comparing the number of languages across macroareas",
    caption = "TidyTuesday | Week 11 | Author: Apiu | November 13, 2026"
  ) +
  #adds more colors 
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "grey40"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 9)
  )
 


```
Research Question
#How similar are languages structurally across families and macro-regions?

The visualization above uses data from the Grambank dataset, which explores the grammatical structures of more than 2,400 languages worldwide. Using a geom_col() chart, the visualization explores how languages differ across language families and geographical regions, including Africa, North America, South America, and other continents. It highlights the distribution of language families across different regions and helps us understand the grammatical diversity of languages around the world.
